title: Night Fire Rescue
description: Firefighters with the Michigan Air National Guard, New York ANG, the Estonian air force and the Latvian air force practice live fire rescue training at the Alpena Combat Readiness Training Center, Michigan, Aug. 13, 2021. State and coalition partners frequently travel to the Alpena Combat Readiness Training Center due to its unique training environment, said Chief Master Sgt. Jeremy Wohlford, the Alpena CRTC fire chief. (U.S. Air National Guard video by Staff Sgt. Joseph Pagan)
keywords: joint force, National All-Domain Warfighting Center, Northern Strike 21, National Guard, exercise

transcript.text: This is live aircraft rescue
firefighting . So the first step was we
were doing an actual response to an
aircraft fire . So the trucks would
pull up the firefighters jump out ,
they grab all the attack lines ,
stretch them out and charge them to get
ready to attack the pool fires that
were outside the aircraft . So in this
room , as we control everything , we
can light the fires up , shut them off ,
plus control all the safety measures ,
just something to go wrong when you
shut it down rather quickly . But the
entire brains of the operation is right
here up in this control room . You know ,
I got a great team of guys . We can
come up with any type of scenario that
your imagination can come up with and
try to meet that , that training
requirement for any fire department out
there .

pass_reason: Live-fire firefighting training at a training center, no real incident.
